title: Accumulate Local Sovereign Capabilities Through Gated Sequential Adapter Updates
target_platform: Apple Silicon M1 (16GB) MLX LoRA training; forging-sovereign-models; 10 GiB RAM ceiling
hypothesis: Across three sequential domain updates, a replay-based LoRA adapter pipeline will: (a) improve newest-domain success by >= 10 percentage points over the frozen initial model after each update; (b) lose <= 3 percentage points on every earlier domain (catastrophic forgetting prevention); (c) reject 100% of deliberately regressive candidate adapters in the promotion gate; and (d) complete each update within 6 hours, using <= 10 GiB process-tree memory and <= 1 GiB incremental swap on 16GB Apple Silicon.
falsification_criteria: Fail if any update violates capability or retention thresholds, a regressive adapter is promoted, or resource limits cannot be met. A smaller model or easier task substitution after evaluation begins requires a new hypothesis.
experiment: Run a feasibility pilot, then freeze one model small enough for the hardware budget. Evaluate three sequential domains with untouched held-outs and three training seeds. Compare frozen weights, naive sequential tuning, and replay plus promotion gates. Include retrieval-assisted frozen-model results as an economic comparator.

model_routing.frontier_escalation_condition: Escalate to bounded standard review solely for validating promotion test manifests (ceiling 250k cloud tokens, 54 training hours).
